task: A group of clinics sends its insurance claims to finance as one raw export, and finance keeps finding claims counted twice, money that doesn't add up and visits that can't be traced. Build a small lakehouse: land the raw claims in Bronze with their provenance, quarantine the ones that break the contract, clean them into Silver, enrich them with the visits and providers, and publish a Gold summary as a Delta table, with a quality report that proves every layer adds up.
problems: Claims repeated exactly by the export.
Claims resubmitted under a new claim id for the same visit, later.
Claims whose provider isn't in the providers table, and claims with no provider at all.
Claims whose service date is after the date they were submitted.
Visit temperatures sent in Fahrenheit instead of Celsius.
A column added to the visits feed on 1 January 2026: older visits have nothing in it.
revenue: Each visit has one claim that counts: the one submitted last. A claim's money is billed (what the clinic asked for), allowed (what the payer agreed, missing until it decides) and paid (what arrived, 0.00 until then). Gold adds up the counting claims only, so its totals must equal Silver's.
